Generate patient trajectories from imported cohort intervals

createTrajectories.Rd

Apply the configured selection, transition and gap rules to a successful study import. The analyst defines clinical states and their intervals. The target cohort supplies the observation bounds.

Usage

createTrajectories(
  cdm = NULL,
  studyEnv = NULL,
  trajectoryType = studyEnv$trajectoryType,
  runSavedStudy = studyEnv$runSavedStudy,
  oocFix = studyEnv$oocFix,
  outOfCohortAllowed = studyEnv$outOfCohortAllowed,
  lengthOfStay = studyEnv$lengthOfStay,
  stateCohortLabels = studyEnv$stateCohortLabels,
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = studyEnv$stateCohortPriorityOrder,
  stateSelectionType = studyEnv$stateSelectionType,
  stateCohortAbsorbing = studyEnv$stateCohortAbsorbing,
  stateCohortMandatory = studyEnv$stateCohortMandatory,
  allowedStatesList = studyEnv$allowedStatesList,
  useCDM = studyEnv$useCDM,
  pathToStudy = studyEnv$pathToStudy,
  batchSize = studyEnv$batchSize,
  mergedStateOverrides = studyEnv$mergedStateOverrides
)

Arguments

cdm

A CDM reference created with CDMConnector, required when joining demographics with useCDM = TRUE.

studyEnv

Study environment returned by cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration.

trajectoryType

Trajectory format, either "Discrete" or "Continuous". Names are case-insensitive. Numeric choice codes are not accepted.

runSavedStudy

Whether to use restored saved-study settings. Import fresh data first. Saved runs do not accept analysis-setting overrides.

oocFix

Discrete gap rule. Use "None" or "OUT OF COHORT" to leave gaps unresolved, "Last present state" to carry an allowed state forward, or a state label as a fallback. See Details for label requirements.

outOfCohortAllowed

Whether retained records may extend the target interval's end. The target start is unchanged.

lengthOfStay

Positive whole-number cycle length in days for discrete trajectories. Use 7 for weekly cycles. Continuous output does not use it.

stateCohortLabels

Nonblank, non-missing clinical state labels, unique ignoring case. The labels "0", "START", "EXIT" and "OUT OF COHORT" are reserved, also ignoring case.

stateCohortPriorityOrder

State labels ordered from highest to lowest priority. Required for all discrete methods and continuous Priority.

stateSelectionType

Selection method, either "First", "Overlap" or "Priority". Names are case-insensitive. A method must be specified.

stateCohortAbsorbing

Labels of states that end a trajectory when retained. In nonmerged studies, use the exact spelling of a configured state, observed state or named discrete fallback. NULL and character(0) mean no absorbing states. Configured states may be absent from the data.

stateCohortMandatory

Mandatory states used by the successful import. Rerun getDataForStudy to change them. Order and duplicates do not matter. NULL and character(0) both mean no requirements.

allowedStatesList

Named list of allowed destinations for each source state. Use one unique, nonempty, non-missing source name per entry, such as list(A = c("B", "C")). An empty list imposes no restrictions.

useCDM

Whether to join age and gender from the supplied CDM. Otherwise, age and gender_concept_id contain NA. No birth date is assumed or added.

pathToStudy

Directory containing the study folder. Generation uses the location stored in studyEnv.

batchSize

Positive whole-number maximum patients per batch.

mergedStateOverrides

List of mergedState() definitions that replace selected inherited properties of merged states.

Value

A data frame of trajectory rows, also saved as a CSV in the study's Data directory. See the output vignette for the complete schema.

Details

In discrete mode, First selects the earliest-starting eligible interval in a cycle. Overlap selects the state covering the most distinct days in that cycle, combining intervals without double-counting shared days. Both methods use the priority order to resolve ties. Priority selects the highest-ranked eligible state present during any part of the cycle. Every clinical state in the bounded input must appear in the priority order.

In continuous mode, First and Overlap both retain intervals that pass the transition rules, including overlaps. Priority assigns shared days to the highest-ranked eligible state and can split lower-priority intervals. It also requires every clinical state to appear in the priority order. Uninterrupted selected intervals do not require self-transitions at unrelated record boundaries. Gaps are not filled and simultaneous records keep their dates. Models requiring unique event times need an explicit tie-handling rule.

Transition rules use the last retained clinical state. Rejected records do not change that state. Source names must use the exact clinical labels. Destination matching is case-insensitive. In a nonempty rule list, each source used for a transition needs an entry. For merged studies, a nonempty list must include every original state, including absorbing states. character(0) permits no destinations. The first clinical state and boundary markers need no incoming rule. Only an allowed, retained absorbing state can end follow-up before the observation boundary.

For discrete gaps, carry-forward requires an allowed self-transition and a named fallback must be an allowed destination. Otherwise the cycle remains OUT OF COHORT. This means no selected state, not loss of observation, and does not reset the last retained state for later transition checks. Supply one nonempty oocFix string. "None" and "Last present state" always select gap-handling behavior, even if a clinical state has that label. Boundary labels "0", "START" and "EXIT" are not valid fallbacks. Use the exact spelling of an existing label. A new label must not differ only in case from an existing clinical or merged-state label. For merged states, use the display label rather than state_key. Declare key-like text in stateCohortLabels if it is intended as a separate literal state.

Boundaries and timing

The first target interval, labelled 0 in cleaned data, supplies the start and end boundaries. Patients without clinical state records remain eligible unless mandatory-state requirements exclude them. Discrete cycles include both endpoint dates, and the final cycle is shortened at the observation boundary. A selected absorbing state stops generation after its cycle. The cycle is not independently shortened to that state's original onset date.

Continuous trajectories end at the retained absorbing interval's end date. Earlier overlapping intervals are capped at that endpoint. START and EXIT are boundary markers and do not add observed time. EXIT is on the day after the last discrete cycle or continuous follow-up endpoint. Its time_in_cohort is elapsed years from trajectory start, using 365.25 days per year.

Setting outOfCohortAllowed = TRUE can extend the endpoint using retained state records, but cannot recover records removed during import. Public imports require a target row for each included patient. The package does not infer observation coverage, episode duration or clinical history. An analyst-defined history-specific terminal state preserves its category when selected, but a discrete row does not retain exact event dates or ordering within its cycle.

Study workflow

Run getDataForStudy successfully before generation. An unsuccessful import blocks generation until a later import succeeds. Existing output files are preserved but are not reused for that failed attempt. The trajectory CSV is written only after all patient batches finish, so a batch error does not replace a previous complete file with a partial result.

A completed fresh run saves Settings/analysisSettings.rds in version 4 format. This preserves analysis settings and any imported CDM definition contents, not patient data. NULL, character(0) and nested lists retain their R types. Only version 4 snapshots are accepted. Saved runs restore their analysis rules and require fresh input. Configure a new study to change those rules.

Labels and identifiers

State IDs are assigned once per study. In unmerged studies, START has ID 1, followed by configured states in their supplied order, additional input and discrete gap labels in alphabetical order, then EXIT. Configured states keep their IDs when absent from a batch. Merged studies use dictionary order and add state_key to the output. Their stateDictionary is available in studyEnv and Data/stateDictionary.rds. Use keys and membership for cross-site comparison rather than run-local state IDs. Original-state rules remain unchanged in the configuration.

Patient IDs are mapped internally and restored before demographic joins and output. File and CDM input preserve large identifiers and leading zeros as text. Canonical numeric IDs below 2^53 retain numeric output. Supply larger in-memory IDs as character or integer64 because doubles may already have rounded them. When reading exported CSVs, read subject_id as character to preserve long or zero-prefixed identifiers. Temporary IDs are not exported.

Working labels and rules are converted to UTF-8 without changing spelling or case. Configuration and saved settings retain the supplied labels.

See also

vignette("a03_trajectories", package = "Cohort2Trajectory"), vignette("a05_output", package = "Cohort2Trajectory")

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
} # }
